cards.a: 1 barely visible left dot - around David
cards.note: This very small dot to the left is common north and west of David.
A small cluster of dirt on the car can be found on the eastern road.
This car with a small stain to the right is only found between Gualaca District and Changuinola.
In a lot of central Panama, the Google car will have either one or two black dots visible on the front.
The region around Changuinola is filled with banana plantations.
Road 50 is the only one in Panama to have a bike lane, from Pesé to Chitre
Cerro Trinidad is a recognizable mountain with exposed rocky slopes west of Capira.
Highway 9 going from Panama City north to Colón is a divided concrete highway. The road is visibly grainy and has a lot of tar lines. The landscape is lush and hilly.

Highway 41 is one of the 6 divided highways of the country. It is pretty easy to recognize because it is the one going to the Barù volcano, so it is sloping and the volcano is visible 90% of the time.
Cities of Changuinola, Torres Bluff and Guabito name their suburbs the same way : “(Finca) Las XX” ,“XX” being the suburb number. They are the only cities where it is done that way.

cards.a: flat, brown or orange soil - around Aguadulce
cards.note: The region around Aguadulce is relatively flat and features a lot of agricultural fields along with very brown or orange soil.
The area around David is very flat, with lots of fairly open fields. Usually, mountains will be visible to the north and northeast.

Road 407 from Boca Chica to the junction with the panamerican highway has been concreted recently. Some parts of it are still dirt and under construction while some are concreted with dotted road lines.

cards.a: High altitude + dry mountains - Ngäbe-Buglé province
cards.note: The main covered road in the Ngäbe-Buglé province is very high-altitude and almost above the clouds. The surrounding mountains tend to be quite dry, and the altitude makes for many stunning views.
Many poles in the western provinces will have horizontal plates attached to them. However, if one of these is accompanied by an eastern vertical plate, the eastern plate takes precedence.

cards.a: Lowered Antenna - mostly Colon and Panama City
cards.note: The antenna can be seen folded down, most commonly in Colón and Panamá provinces, and occasionally in the city of David.

cards.a: Lush green + overcast -  road going to Changuinola
cards.note: The road going to Changuinola features a lush and green hilly landscape. The weather is cloudy or overcast on the entire road.

cards.a: Meseta de Chorcha - east of David
cards.note: On a small stretch of the panamerican highway east of David, a rocky formation, Meseta de Chorcha, can be seen. It is a very distinct elevation point and is unique in this region.

MOP-sticker -The sticker is always black and small -Only in these 5 states, but for Coclé and Veraguas there by far mostly in the south of the state and in Chiriqui not that common -The highway in southern Veraguas almost has this sticker on every sign

MOP-paint -This again reads ‘MOP’ with its logo and all. This time it has a lot of text above the logo -The difference, obviously, is that it's black paint (not a sticker) and it's very big -Only on the green part of the CA-1 in Darién but this time it's on most of the signs along the road
Phone codes starting with 2 are found in Panama City and the east.
Phone codes starting with 4 are found in Colon.

cards.a: Phone Code 7 - Bocas del Toro & Chiriquí
cards.note: Phone codes starting with 7 are found in the west.
Phone codes starting with 9 are found in Coclé, Herrera, Los Santos & Veraguas.

cards.a: Red dot on the right - Panamá Oeste & road 2
cards.note: This small red spot can mostly be found in Panamá Oeste and on the road 2 going from southern Los Santos province to the Verguas province. Note: Road 2 is the only divided road with this car.
Sunset coverage can be found in southern Panama on a small road south of Tonosi. The more south you go, the lower the sun.

Just like Colombian taxis, taxis in Panama are yellow and have the name of the city/province labeled on them. It is sometimes hard to read Panama Taxis plates, especially the name of the province/city.

cards.a: Thin yellow plate - mostly Colón Province
cards.note: Thin yellow plates, vertical or horizontal, with a visible black border are most common in the Colón Province.

cards.a: Triangle dots - Southwest of Panama City
cards.note: This triangle of dots on the front right of the car is common southwest of the capital.

cards.a: Tropical landscape - around Colón and Panama City
cards.note: Green tropical landscapes with palm trees and very tall grass are common around Colón and Panama City.
The eastern provinces often have tall vertical plates that can be yellow or white. They are commonly attached to poles by black zip ties.
Volcanic rocks that are either scattered on the ground, or built into rock walls, are common north of David.

cards.a: Volcanic rock + dry + pines - Northeast of Volcán
cards.note: A mountainous landscape with pine trees, volcanic rocks, dry grass, and gravel roads can be found northeast of Volcán.
Colón features a lot of warehouses and rundown multi-storey buildings.

cards.a: White high rise buildings - Panama City
cards.note: Panama City can be recognised by the large number of white high-rise buildings.
Northern: in the mountains, southern: in a flat area
Yellow pole socks can be found near the Panama Canal, around the town of Gatún.
